title: Canonical change of geometric point on strict localizations
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme and let $x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_1\to S$ and $y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_2\to S$ be geometric points [def-weil-geometric-point]. Write $S_{(x)},S_{(y)}$ for their strict localizations [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit], $\rho_x,\rho_y$ for their structural maps [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-structural-map], and $\epsilon_x:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_1\to S_{(x)}$, $\epsilon_y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_2\to S_{(y)}$ for the spectra of the canonical evaluation homomorphisms [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-point-evaluation]. For an isomorphism $e:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_1\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{Spec}\Omega_2$ with $y\circ e=x$, the canonical change-of-point map $e^{\mathrm{loc}}:S_{(x)}\to S_{(y)}$ is the unique morphism $h$ satisfying $\rho_y\circ h=\rho_x$ and $h\circ\epsilon_x=\epsilon_y\circ e$. Such a unique morphism exists; it is obtained by precomposing pointed etale neighbourhoods with $e$ and using the limit universal property.
